abstract: We present two mixed-factorial experimental studies that examine the use of computer-generated speech reading long-form professional, declarative content in the context of car reviews and weather reports. We investigate the effect of perceived age and gender of synthetic voices on four variables: competence, informativeness, quality, and credibility. The long-form professional, declarative content presented by an older synthetic voice was perceived as less credible and of lower quality, with the older synthetic voice perceived as less competent and informative. The findings from these studies indicate that age stereotypes may be replicated in people's interactions with synthetic voices and that age-stereotypes may outweigh gender stereotypes when using computer-generated speech to convey professional, declarative long-form content. These findings fill an empirical gap in the literature about the complex interplay of age and gender-based stereotypes in computer-generated speech, providing directions for further research and development of future voice-based technologies.

ur.tldr: 两项混合因子实验考察年龄与性别线索如何影响用户对专业声明性合成语音的评价。老年语音在汽车评论和天气报告中获得的可信度、质量、能力及信息性评价更低，年龄刻板印象的影响超过性别刻板印象。

title: An Investigation of Age and Gender Stereotypes in Professional, Declarative Uses of Computer-Generated Speech
title_zh: 计算机生成语音的专业性与陈述性用法中的年龄和性别刻板印象研究
